findings.title: Materials' 59-Point Lens Gap Signals Distress
findings.body: Materials' trailing P/E sits at the 91st percentile while its forward multiple is only at the 32nd, a 59-point spread that is the widest in the table. This implies the market expects a 126 percent earnings surge, a bet that looks overly optimistic given the sector's current valuation extremes.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' Forward Cheapness Masks Rich History
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward P/E has plunged 31 percentile points in a month to the 13th percentile, yet its trailing multiple remains at the 77th percentile. This 64-point gap between lenses suggests the market is pricing in a dramatic earnings rebound, but the sector's historical valuation still looks stretched.

findings.title: Utilities' Zero Percentile Hides Steep De-Rating
findings.body: Utilities now trades at its cheapest forward multiple in five years, with a 15-point weekly drop pushing it to the 0th percentile. The 33 percent compression between trailing and forward earnings implies a 48 percent profit recovery, yet the sector's defensive appeal may be fading as rate expectations shift.
